tagline: Leading global provider of IT services helping clients simplify, optimize, and modernize their systems
hero_kpi_rationale: The book-to-bill ratio is the hero KPI as it directly reflects demand dynamics in IT services, with strong acceleration in fiscal 2025 (1.03x vs 0.91x), signaling a recovery in client commitments following a period of contraction.

kpis.name: Book-to-bill Ratio
kpis.explanation: Measures the ratio between new orders signed and annual revenue.
kpis.description: A ratio above 1x indicates the company is signing more contracts than it is recognizing in revenue, a sign of future growth.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from IT services.
kpis.description: Revenue declined by 5.8% in fiscal 2025, but the decline is moderating in constant currency (-4.8%) and organic terms (-4.6%).

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of services, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved by 150 basis points due to reduced service-related costs and optimization of service delivery.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin remained stable at around 7.9% despite revenue contraction, reflecting the effectiveness of cost-reduction initiatives.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from operations after capital expenditures.
kpis.description: $687 million of FCF in fiscal 2025 (cash from operations of $1.398B minus capex of $711M), despite revenue decline, driven by strong cost and working capital management.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.description: Over 120,000 employees across more than 60 countries, reflecting DXC's global operational scale.
kpis.signal: Critical scale for global IT services

kpis.name: GBS Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Consulting, Engineering and Software segment.
kpis.description: The GBS segment declined less than GIS (-2.6% vs -9.1%), driven by AI and engineering services.

kpis.name: GIS Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the managed IT infrastructure segment.
kpis.description: The GIS segment faces significant contraction, reflecting client transition to cloud and more modern models.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and security breaches
risks.score_rationale: DXC is vulnerable to cyberattacks, which could compromise critical client systems and data, having a material impact on its business and reputation. Threats are becoming increasingly sophisticated.

risks.title: Regulatory non-compliance on data
risks.score_rationale: DXC must comply with strict data protection and privacy laws and regulations. Non-compliance could result in fines, penalties, and reputational damage.

risks.title: Client data loss
risks.score_rationale: DXC stores and processes sensitive data for its clients, making it vulnerable to data loss. Such an event could have a material impact on its business and reputation.

risks.title: Increased competitive intensity
risks.score_rationale: DXC operates in a highly competitive market, which could affect its business and financial performance. The company must innovate and differentiate to maintain its market position.

risks.title: High debt and refinancing risk
risks.score_rationale: DXC carries significant debt, which could affect its ability to invest and fund operations. Rising interest rates or credit rating downgrades could increase debt costs.

risks.title: Reputation-related risks
risks.score_rationale: DXC is exposed to reputation risks, particularly in cases of non-compliance, data loss, or cyberattacks. Reputational damage could materially impact its business.

risks.title: Cloud transition and legacy service obsolescence
risks.score_rationale: The GIS segment, focused on traditional managed infrastructure services, is experiencing a 9.1% decline due to client migration to cloud and modern models, representing a significant structural risk.

ai_positioning.summary: DXC is integrating AI into its service offerings, particularly in the GBS segment with Consulting Engineering Services (CES) focused on AI and data analytics, and AI-powered insurance solutions to optimize client operations.
evidence: CES helps businesses use artificial intelligence (AI) and data analytics to improve operations, automate tasks, and speed up their digital transformation
advanced AI-powered solutions that enhances operational efficiency, improves customer experiences, and enables insurers to adopt a digital-first approach
